name: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Associated with Chronic Inflammation
aliases: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma arising in Chronic Inflammatory Background

ethnicAssociations: More common in East Asian populations
Reported in patients with longstanding pyothorax or chronic osteomyelitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse proliferation of large atypical B-cells with immunoblastic or centroblastic morphology
Evidence of lymphoma arising in a site of longstanding chronic inflammation (e.g., pyothorax, chronic osteomyelitis)
Detection of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in tumor cells by in situ hybridization or immunohistochemistry
Expression of B-cell markers (CD20, CD79a) and high proliferation index (Ki-67)
Exclusion of other lymphoma subtypes by morphology and immunophenotyping

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in a site of chronic inflammation with EBV positivity in tumor cells
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical history, histopathology, EBV status, and immunophenotyping

pathognomonic.symptomName: Painless enlarging mass at site of chronic inflammation
pathognomonic.notes: Typically arises in pleural cavity or bone with chronic inflammation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of systemic 'B' symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
searchTerms: systemic symptoms like chills and weight loss
B symptoms including fever and sweating

common.symptomName: Localized swelling and induration over chronic inflammatory site
Fatigue related to anemia of chronic disease
searchTerms: fatigue due to low red blood cells
weakness from anemia of chronic disease

occasional.symptomName: Pleural effusion in cases involving pyothorax
Bone pain in cases arising from chronic osteomyelitis
searchTerms: bone pain from chronic bone infection
small lymph node swelling near affected area

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to mass effect or infiltration
searchTerms: nerve problems due to tumor pressure
brain or nerve symptoms from infiltration

laboratory: EBV-encoded RNA (EBER) positivity in tumor cells
imaging: CT or MRI showing mass lesion at site of chronic inflammation
Pleural thickening or effusion in pyothorax-associated cases
genetic: No consistent chromosomal translocations, but frequent complex karyotypes
EBV genome detected in tumor cells
other: Histopathology showing large atypical B-cells with immunoblastic morphology
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, CD79a, and high Ki-67 proliferation index

distinguishingFeatures: Overlap with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with chronic inflammation
Requires demonstration of EBV positivity and chronic inflammation site
May be considered a subtype rather than separate entity
Usually presents as lymphomatous effusion without mass
Associated with HHV-8 infection rather than EBV
Usually lacks EBV positivity in all cases

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mass in a site of chronic inflammation
Unexplained systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Evidence of EBV positivity in tumor cells from biopsy
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Kamada N, et al. Pyothorax-associated lymphoma: a distinct clinicopathologic entity. Cancer. 1994.
Nakamura S, et al. EBV-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma associated with chronic inflammation. Blood. 2008.
